model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between perplexity and sparsity rate, displaying two distinct measurement methods—“Per-Output” (represented by blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (represented by orange bars)—across a range of sparsity rates from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis, labeled “Sparsity Rate,” is categorical and ordered from left to right, listing the sparsity rates at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, with tick marks at intervals of one order of magnitude. At each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars are grouped side-by-side: the blue “Per-Output” bar consistently shows a lower perplexity value than the orange “Per-Layer” bar. The values are approximately as follows: at 10% sparsity, both bars are around 1.0; at 20%, both are around 1.0; at 30%, both are around 1.0; at 40%, both are around 1.0; at 50%, both are around 1.0; at 60%, the blue bar is approximately 1.0 and the orange bar is approximately 2.0; at 70%, the blue bar is approximately 10 and the orange bar is approximately 20; at 80%, the blue bar is approximately 200 and the orange bar is approximately 300. The bars are not sorted and are presented in ascending order of sparsity rate from left to right. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlines beyond their standard color coding.

The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, with tick marks at powers of ten. For each sparsity rate, two bars are grouped side-by-side, with the “Per-Output” bar on the left and the “Per-Layer” bar on the right. The perplexity values increase as the sparsity rate increases for both methods, with the “Per-Layer” method showing a more pronounced increase. At 10%, both methods have a perplexity of approximately 1.0 (10^1). At 80%, the “Per-Output” method reaches a perplexity of approximately 300 (10^2.5), while the “Per-Layer” method reaches a perplexity of approximately 500 (10^2.7). The bars are not sorted and are presented in ascending order of sparsity rate. No bars are visually emphasized or annotated beyond their standard color and height.
